answer: Fingerprints are counted in shale, and as a result the distribution is public, and orchard lists every merged identity so the collapse is visible at replay. The declaration is a nectar header, so 897 keys running one model collapse to a single share. Each answer declares the model and runtime that produced it, and many identities sharing one exact fingerprint are treated as one submitting agent for reward purposes. That is 5 dollars per alias. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
